habit: Buys after a stock has already run up: about 60% of buys come after a rise of 10% or more in the 20 trading days before, on stocks first looked at before the rise.

name: Chasing price rises
signals: Buys made after the price had risen since your first look did -6.5 pts against those made after a fall.
On your buy days the NASDAQ was stronger than on 61% of all trading days.

name: Trading more than your information supports
signals: You turn over 265% of your depot a year; the average private investor in Barber & Odean's data turned over about 75%.

text: Do not buy a stock that has already risen more than 30% in the last 30 days. Wait for a pullback, or skip it.
Do not place buys in the morning (6-11 h on your clock). Decide then if you like, and place the order at another time.
Do not buy while the market is as turbulent as on the most turbulent 10% of days (volatility above about 27% a year).
Do more research before you buy: look at the stock on at least about 3 occasions in the 30 days before (a conviction score of 1, the number on the watchlist's pills).
After selling, wait at least 3 days before you buy something else with the money. Switches you made faster did worse than what you sold.
Do not buy a stock whose 12-month return is in the top 20% of the stocks you viewed in the last 30 days.
Keep a buy in a lottery stock (a day above +10% in the last month, or a cheap, very volatile stock) to at most 1x your usual buy.
When you have looked at a stock on fewer than about 3 occasions in the last 30 days (a conviction score under 1), keep the buy to at most 0.5x your usual buy.
